page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 24 dedicated vCPUs and 12 physical cores running at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 93.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per core. It features a single NVIDIA T4 GPU based on the Turing architecture with 16 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and network performance is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between CPU and GPU-accelerated workloads. Single-core CPU performance is positioned in the lower tier, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25 percent, and single-threaded gzip compression performing in the bottom 10 percent. However, multi-core performance is average, as demonstrated by PassMark and Geekbench multi-core tests. The server excels in GPU-driven tasks, particularly in LLM inference where prompt processing for both small and medium models ranks in the top 10 percent, achieving 8377.38 and 1130.26 tokens per second respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the premium cost of high-end tensor-core accelerators. The primary tradeoff is the lower single-core CPU performance and the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes. This makes the instance less suitable for heavy single-threaded processing or disk-I/O intensive tasks that require low-latency local storage.

The ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is optimized for workloads that can leverage GPU acceleration, such as small to medium LLM inference, machine learning model deployment, video transcoding, and moderate parallel computing tasks. It is also suitable for general-purpose workloads that require a dedicated GPU alongside standard multi-core processing capabilities.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.6xlarge is an x86_64 GPU-accelerated server featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8163 processor, 93.0 GB of RAM, and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It includes a single NVIDIA T4 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, while local storage is absent. Performance benchmarks show weak single-core CPU capabilities but average multi-core and memory bandwidth results. Crucially, the instance delivers top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing, making it highly efficient for deploying smaller AI models. Qualitatively, it serves as a cost-effective option for GPU-driven workloads, trading off raw single-threaded CPU speed and local storage for affordable parallel processing. It is best suited for machine learning inference, video encoding, and GPU-assisted general-purpose workloads.
